issue_context.title: Index out of range [1] with length 1 when using AES_DECRYPT
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report
Index out of range [1] with length 1 when using AES_DECRYPT

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)
```
create table test (name1 varchar(64),name2 varchar(64));
insert into test values('99FAFD8059A44BC14BCCC70154AC00F3','99FAFD8059A44BC14BCCC70154AC00F3');
SELECT * FROM test WHERE CAST(AES_DECRYPT(UNHEX(name1), 'r��Lu-t�AS�h)%R`') AS CHAR) = '00' AND CAST(AES_DECRYPT(UNHEX(name2), 'r��`') AS CHAR) = '1';
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
No error

ERROR 1105 (HY000): runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1

comments: The first `EQ` expr filter all rows(`Sel` in `Chunk` is not nil, but length is zero, check [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/util/chunk/chunk.go#L347)), but `builtinAesDecrypt` in the second `EQ` expr assume the result of its child result is not empty, and try to get the first byte of its child result(check [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/expression/builtin_encryption_vec.go#L73)). So we got this panic.
You can disble vectorized expr(`set @@tidb_enable_vectorized_expression = off `) as a workround

review_comments: Maybe add a comment to explain why add check `n == 0` explicitly, because normally we handle `n == 0` in the `for loop` implicitly .
